name: Gangotri Glacier & Upper Ganga
summary: Glacial source of the sacred Bhagirathi river undergoing accelerated recession, threatening dry-season baseflow for millions downstream.

hotspots.title: Gaumukh Snout & Proglacial Moraine Dam
hotspots.description: Glacial terminus at 4,000m where Bhagirathi emerges, surrounded by unconsolidated lateral moraines.
hotspots.impactCarryOn: Glacier snout retreats over 45 meters per year, expanding unstable moraine lakes that threaten sudden outburst floods.
hotspots.impactProtect: Glacial melting stabilizes with snout retreat slowing to under 14 meters per year, preserving seasonal ice buffers.

hotspots.title: Gangotri Temple Town & Pilgrim Ghats
hotspots.description: Sacred shrine town hosting over 500,000 pilgrims during the annual Char Dham Yatra pilgrimage.
hotspots.impactCarryOn: Bhagirathi dry-season lean flow drops by 52%, leaving holy bathing ghats and pilgrim water intakes dry before monsoon.
hotspots.impactProtect: Protected upper-catchment forestry and check dams maintain steady perennial river baseflow for downstream pilgrims.

hotspots.title: Harsil Valley Terraced Apple Orchards
hotspots.description: High-altitude Himalayan valley villages reliant on snowmelt channels for terraced fruit orchards.
hotspots.impactCarryOn: Winter snowfall deficits and early spring heat force farmers to abandon low-altitude orchards, driving village out-migration.
hotspots.impactProtect: Community snow-harvesting reservoirs and micro-sprinklers safeguard terraced orchards and village livelihoods.

carryOn.description: Rapid loss of Himalayan glacial mass leads to initial flash flooding followed by severe pre-monsoon drying across the entire upper Ganga river basin.
keyPoints: Gaumukh retreats more than 3.5 kilometers upstream by 2100
Pre-monsoon river volume drops by over 50%, curtailing hydro-power and drinking water
Fragile moraine dam failures elevate catastrophic glacial outburst flood risks

protect.description: Meeting Paris climate thresholds curtails high-altitude warming, allowing glacier accumulation zones to stabilize while alpine watershed work protects river flow.
keyPoints: Glacial recession rate slows to under 14 meters annually, preserving long-term ice mass
Regenerated birch and alpine rhododendron buffers reduce slope erosion into river channels
Sustainable pilgrimage regulations protect fragile high-altitude ecological equilibrium
